sources.title: Community District Boundaries
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
transformations: polygons simplified for display (Douglas-Peucker, 15 m)

sources.title: Ward Boundaries
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
transformations: each home placed in the ward that contains it (point in polygon)

sources.title: Current Year Property Assessments (Parcel)
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
sources.unit: one assessed residential property (a house, a townhouse or a condominium unit)
transformations: each record placed at the mean of its parcel outline's vertices
records listed in the unit-weights file count as their number of units
564 rental buildings outside the residential filter added by roll number (620 rows read); 3 buildings listed in the weights file were not found on the current roll and are not counted

sources.title: Rental building units (Calgary Data Desk growth model input, built 28 October 2026)
sources.publisher: Calgary Data Desk (Hassan Ali), derived from City of Calgary open data
sources.licence: Derived from open data under the publisher's licence
limitations: Purpose-built rental buildings are one record each on the roll. Their units are taken from matching building permits (658 buildings, 43,677 units) or estimated from assessed value (1,569 buildings, 32,163 units). Records missing from the residential filter are read by roll number.
transformations: joined to the roll by roll number

sources.title: Playground Equipment
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
limitations: City-maintained play structures only; school, developer and condominium playgrounds that are not in the City's inventory are not counted.
sources.query: type_description='MULTI PLAY COMPLEX' AND life_cycle_status in('ACTIVE','INSTALLED')
transformations: distance to the nearest one from every home

sources.title: Parks Sites
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
limitations: Every City park site of any size counts, including small sub-neighbourhood parks and linear parks along pathways.
Parks in new communities may still be held by the developer and missing from the City's inventory.
transformations: distance to the nearest one from every home, to the polygon edge (edges sampled every 20 m)

sources.title: Calgary Transit Stops
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
limitations: A stop is not a service level: how often buses come is not measured here (planned: the GTFS timetable).
transformations: distance to the nearest one from every home

sources.title: Community Services
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
limitations: Community association halls and centres as listed by the City; opening hours and programs are not measured.
transformations: distance to the nearest one from every home

sources.title: Recreation Facilities
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
limitations: Leisure centres, aquatic and fitness centres and fieldhouses, municipal and not-for-profit. Arenas, outdoor pools, golf courses and other single-purpose sites are left out. Capacity and opening hours are not measured.
sources.query: facility_type in('Leisure Centre','Leisure Centre - Municipal','Aquatic & Fitness Centre','Fieldhouse')
transformations: distance to the nearest one from every home

sources.title: Community Services
sources.licence: Open Government Licence - City of Calgary
limitations: Library branches as listed by the City; hours and size are not measured.
transformations: distance to the nearest one from every home

sources.title: OpenStreetMap (Overpass API)
limitations: Volunteer-mapped: coverage is uneven, and a missing feature means nobody has mapped it.
Only features not already in the city's inventory are added (matching rules in the method).
transformations: matched against the city's own playgrounds and park sites; duplicates and features outside every community left out

sources.title: Residents and children by community: City's total, shared by actual growth (Calgary Data Desk)
sources.publisher: Calgary Data Desk (Hassan Ali), from City of Calgary open data, the City's population estimate and the 2021 Census
limitations: Estimates by community from Calgary Data Desk's population model, spread evenly over each community's dwelling units.
Communities with fewer than 100 residents are not included and get no residents or children.
The City's figure for 2026 onward is a forecast (Calgary and Region Economic Outlook, spring 2026).
transformations: each area's residents and children spread evenly over its dwelling units
areas with fewer than 100 residents are not in the source and get none
